fomc-2026-09.standing: The rate-setting meeting of the US central bank's Open Market Committee, held eight times a year to set the federal funds target that anchors dollar borrowing costs worldwide. Credit prices everywhere adjust to it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The committee arrives with the oil shock already in the price index: August consumer prices rose 0.4% after Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha and crude reached $105. Hike odds moved to two-in-three on a payroll surge, and the question is whether a supply shock reaching American mortgages at 6.71% is one the Fed treats as its own.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote individually on Bank Rate roughly eight times a year. Its decisions set the floor under British mortgage costs and savings returns, and sterling moves on the split.
boe-2026-09.recent: Bailey used a G20 appearance to warn that AI could cause a global economic downturn, an unusual framing from a governor whose committee meets amid a bond selloff that has pushed yields to multi-decade highs on inflation fears. The question the vote settles is whether a long-end repricing the Bank does not control changes what it does with the rate it does.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of Japan's vast government debt, and the global carry trade funded by cheap yen.
boj-2026-09.recent: The yen's slide past 160 per dollar has pushed Tokyo to weigh steering the currency with pension money, a 2014 playbook, rather than leaving its defence to the Bank of Japan's rate. With oil at $105 swelling the fuel bill of an import-dependent economy, this meeting settles whether the policy rate joins that defence.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The UK's monthly consumer price index, published by the Office for National Statistics. It is the measure the Bank of England's 2% target is written against, and it sets the uprating of pensions, benefits and index-linked gilts.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The September reading is the one the uprating formula reaches back to, so it fixes next April's pension and benefit rises rather than merely describing a month. It lands after a run of releases elsewhere in which energy costs did the work — petrol drove the sharp US increase in August — leaving the committee to separate a fuel pass-through from the domestic services prices it can actually reach.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the US federal funds rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. It is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt reprice against it.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee arrives at this one arguing about a supply shock it cannot reach: oil at $105 after Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, feeding an August CPI print of 0.4%, while a payroll surge removed the labour-market slack that would justify looking through it. Warsh has flagged the trap — imported inflation transmitted through the dollar, with emerging-market debt on the other side.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the single policy rate for the twenty countries that use the euro. One decision has to fit economies as different as Germany's exporters and Greece's borrowers, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The council meets after an energy shock that has pushed forecasters to mark up where the ECB stops rather than when it starts cutting — Deutsche Bank now puts the peak rate at 2.75%. What it settles is whether Frankfurt treats fuel costs feeding into wages and services as second-round transmission it must lean against, or a price level it looks through.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set Japan's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, government bond yields and the carry trades that borrow in yen to invest abroad.
boj-2026-10.recent: The yen slid past 160 per dollar, and Tokyo is now weighing Japan's 2014 playbook: steering the currency through pension money rather than the policy rate. This meeting settles whether the Bank of Japan leaves the yen's defence to that channel or takes part of the job back with its own rate.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its votes are published individually, and they set the price of credit for British households, most of whom refinance a fixed mortgage every two to five years.
boe-2026-11.recent: Bailey has spent the run-up arguing a case outside the rate itself, telling the G20 that AI could cause a global economic downturn. The committee meets into a bond market that has pushed yields to multi-decade highs on inflation fears, and with oil at $105 — a supply shock Bank Rate cannot reach, landing on borrowers who reprice on a short fixed cycle.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the twelve-member body that sets the US federal funds rate eight times a year. The rate it chooses is the reference price for dollar credit worldwide, and borrowing costs from mortgages to emerging-market debt reprice against it.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee arrives at this meeting arguing about a supply shock it cannot reach: Houthi fighters captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil jumped to $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4%. A payroll surge has moved hike odds to two-in-three, and Warsh faces the trap of tightening into imported inflation while the 30-year mortgage rate sits at 6.71%.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of heads of state and government from nineteen countries plus the European and African Unions, hosted by a rotating presidency. It sets no binding law, but the communiqué it does or does not agree on marks where the world's largest economies still share a position.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency has already turned its year of hosting into a campaign, with Treasury asking other members to make its case against China's surplus at the Asheville ministerial, where European finance ministers boycotted the family photo over Siluanov's return. Zelensky has said he is ready to meet Putin face-to-face in Miami, and Moscow has not ruled out a Putin-Trump-Xi summit.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the deposit rate for the twenty countries sharing the euro. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing for some 350 million people, and reach every sovereign bond market in the bloc at once.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The question at Frankfurt is no longer when the tightening stops but where it ends: Deutsche Bank has lifted its ECB peak to 2.75%, on the argument that an energy shock is passing into wages and prices rather than fading. That is a second-round problem a central bank is expected to answer, unlike a one-off. This meeting settles how much further the Council is willing to go.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote individually on Bank Rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. The rate sets the floor under British mortgage pricing and business lending, and sterling moves with the vote split.
boe-2026-12.recent: Governor Andrew Bailey went to the G20 warning that AI could cause a global economic downturn — an unusual thing for a central banker to put ahead of the near-term inflation question the committee actually votes on. The meeting also comes with oil at $105 and long-dated government borrowing costs at multi-decade highs worldwide, a squeeze the MPC can do nothing about but must decide whether to lean against.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board, which meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields and the global carry trades funded in cheap yen.
boj-2026-12.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar, and so far Tokyo's response has come from outside the Bank of Japan: Japan is weighing whether to use pension money to steer the currency, echoing a 2014 playbook. This decision settles whether defending the yen stays with that workaround or reaches the policy rate itself.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-09-16.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of sales at US retail and food-service businesses, drawn from a survey of thousands of firms. It is the earliest broad read on household spending, which drives roughly two-thirds of the American economy.
